_doc: Example spec for render_set.py. Paths are relative to this file; keys starting with _ are ignored. Headline emphasis: wrap words in *asterisks*; \n forces a line break. Layouts: device (default), zoom, full, poster. Sizes: render_set.py --presets. The screens are a fictional app built by tools/demo_screens/build.py; example-screens/regions.json lists exact element boxes for crops.
_doc_promise_words: Words from the brief that say what the app does or makes; render_set warns if none of the first three headlines uses one (search shows only those three).
_doc_sizes: ios (1206x2622, required) + ios-large (1320x2868) cover iPhone; android = Google Play 1080x1920; add duo-outer / duo-inner (iPhone Duo) or ipad with screens captured on those devices: "screen": {"default": "…", "duo-inner": "…"}. "stores": ["ios"] on a shot keeps it out of the Play set (the poster here: Play wants in-app screenshots). render_set.py --presets lists all.
_doc_direction: Optional: "direction": "editorial" | "poster" | "playful" | "cinematic" | "crafted" | "native" | "utility" (concepts.py --list). The direction becomes the base look and "style" overrides it, so with a direction keep only the style keys you want to change. See references/directions.md.
_doc_brand: Colour tokens for directions ($primary, $ink, $paper…). Or "brand_from": ["icon.png", "screens/01.png"] to guess them.

style._doc_font: alias (sans, sans-bold, sans-medium, serif, serif-italic, text…) or a path to the brand .ttf/.otf
style._doc_emphasis: style: color (color) | box (color, text_color) | marker (color) | font (font, weight, scale, color)
style._doc_device: style phone|none; width = fraction of canvas width; radius/border = fraction of device width; bleed lets it run off the edge
